title: North Providence weighs tree preservation fund in proposed ordinance update
text:
← Back to the wire
Government
North Providence weighs tree preservation fund in proposed ordinance update
Tree Warden Tim Thorp told the Planning Board the fund would hold donations and fines rather than tax money and would not be zeroed out annually.
The North Providence Planning Board reviewed a proposed tree preservation fund as part of a broader update to the town's tree ordinance during a meeting Thursday, Oct. 15, at North Providence Council Chambers.
THE PROPOSAL Tim Thorp, Tree Warden for North Providence, described the fund as similar to an existing land trust mechanism. "Not diff not terribly different from the land trusts fund," Thorp said, explaining it would not rely on tax dollars but on donations and fines, and would carry over each year rather than being absorbed into the annual budget.
Thorp said he hoped the fund could eventually help residents facing private tree issues. "I would hope it would acrue to a matter where it would be helpful to people who have significant trees," he said.
REGISTRY TIED TO FUND Thorp also proposed a companion measure, a "voluntary significant inherited tree registry," which he said would let residents apply to use money from the fund.
APPROVAL PROCESS Board members noted the fund, like the rest of the ordinance, would need approval from the Town Council. Board Chairman noted that the provision would need to be "ratified by the town council," and Thorp confirmed, "It would. Yeah, that that's how it's proposed to us."
Thorp said he based the fund concept on his own idea rather than a recommendation from an outside group, telling the board the Green Infrastructure Center "liked it" after he developed it. The board took no vote on the fund itself Thursday, asking Thorp instead to return with a document detailing all proposed changes to the ordinance before further discussion.
